Rules

Zylinderfolgeschach.

Ordinary chess, changed by cylindrical geometry and compulsory pursuit.

01 · Cylinder 02 · Follow 03 · King safety 04 · Special moves 05 · Ending
01

The files form a cylinder.

The left and right edges of the board are connected. Movement continues across the a/h seam exactly as if the board were wrapped into a cylinder.

f1–g2–h3–a4–b5–c6–d7–e8A bishop's complete diagonal on an empty board.

Every piece and special move uses this geometry, including knight moves, pawn captures, king attacks, and en passant.

02

Follow when it is legal.

After a move, the square that piece left is the follow field. If the opponent has at least one otherwise legal move whose destination is that square, the opponent must choose one of those moves.

If several pieces can follow, the player chooses among them. If no legal follower exists, every ordinary legal move is available.

03

King safety remains absolute.

A move that leaves or places the moving side's king in check is never legal. An apparent follower that fails to resolve check does not count.

If a player is checked and a legal move to the follow field resolves that check, following is still compulsory. If no such follower exists, the player may choose any legal check evasion.

Attacks count even when the attacking move could not currently be selected because of the follow obligation.

04

Special moves remain.

Castling
Uses the normal safety restrictions. Castling creates no follow field.
Promotion
A pawn that follows onto its last rank promotes normally.
En passant
Works normally and observes the cylindrical seam. The follow field is still the previous move's origin.
05

Checkmate is the objective.

Checkmate and stalemate are determined from the complete ZFS legal move set. Threefold repetition is an automatic draw, as is reaching 100 reversible halfmoves under the 50-move rule.

There is no claim procedure, separate fivefold rule, or 75-move rule.
